pack.title: Interrupters & talk-overs
pack.description: Mid-sentence takeovers in meetings and calls. Finish your point, keep the room.

scenarios.setting: Conference room. You're mid-sentence when a peer talks over you.
scenarios.jab: Yeah yeah — what you're trying to say is—

replies.line: Let me finish this point, then I'll hand over.
replies.why: It makes turn-taking explicit and commits to giving the other person a turn.
replies.delivery: Speak at the same volume, finish the sentence, then genuinely offer the floor.

replies.why: It states the fact plainly and the room does the rest.
replies.delivery: Speak at the same volume, finish the sentence, then genuinely offer the floor.

replies.line: Hold that thought — I'm landing the plane.
replies.why: It uses a shared metaphor to ask for enough time to finish your point.
replies.delivery: Speak at the same volume, finish the sentence, then genuinely offer the floor.

replies.line: Spoilers — I hadn't reached the good part.
replies.why: Casting his interruption as impatience for your ending flips who looks eager.
replies.delivery: Speak at the same volume, finish the sentence, then genuinely offer the floor.

trap.line: God, do you ever let anyone finish?
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Finish your point before handing over the floor.

followUp.jab: I already know where you're going.
followUp.line: Please let me finish; then I'd like your response.
followUp.why: It keeps the turn-taking request clear without speculating about their motive.
followUp.delivery: Speak at the same volume, finish the sentence, then genuinely offer the floor.

scenarios.setting: Client call. You pause to think; a colleague fills it with your point, louder.
scenarios.jab: To build on that — here's the actual takeaway—

replies.line: That's the point from my analysis. Here's the next step.
replies.why: It identifies your contribution without disputing the shared conclusion.
replies.delivery: Stress “my analysis” lightly, then put the main emphasis on the next step.

replies.why: Short, true, and impossible to argue with on a recorded call.
replies.delivery: Say “That was my point” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense. Then put the main emphasis on the next step.

replies.line: Exactly where I was headed — great minds.
replies.why: Agreement absorbs the steal and the client hears you as the source.
replies.delivery: Keep “Exactly where I was headed” warm and unhurried; finish the request clearly. Then put the main emphasis on the next step.

replies.line: Same page; let me finish the next paragraph.
replies.why: Humor recognizes agreement while asking to complete your contribution.
replies.delivery: Keep “Same page” light; let the joke stand without repeating it. Then put the main emphasis on the next step.

trap.line: Stop stealing my ideas on calls.
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Reestablish your contribution without disputing collaboration.

followUp.line: Yes; that's the point from my analysis, and here's the next step.
followUp.why: It names your contribution while moving the shared discussion forward.
followUp.delivery: Stress “my analysis” lightly, then put the main emphasis on the next step.

scenarios.setting: One-on-one. Your manager checks his phone while you talk, then looks up.
scenarios.jab: Sorry — can you start over? I missed all of that.

replies.line: Here's the short version; I'll send the details afterward.
replies.why: It restores the relevant information in a format the remaining time allows.
replies.delivery: Lead with the decision, use one short sentence, then pause for their answer.

replies.why: Three words that end the performance and keep the content intact.
replies.delivery: Lead with the decision, use one short sentence, then pause for their answer.

replies.line: Long story short — here's the one thing I need from you.
replies.why: It rescues the meeting by shrinking your ask to phone-proof size.
replies.delivery: Lead with the decision, use one short sentence, then pause for their answer.

replies.line: Here's the recap; the extended version can go by email.
replies.why: A light format joke offers a practical follow-up rather than punishing distraction.
replies.delivery: Lead with the decision, use one short sentence, then pause for their answer.

trap.line: Forget it. You clearly don't care.
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Recover attention with a concise request.

followUp.jab: I have another meeting in a minute.
followUp.line: Here's the decision I need; I'll send the background afterward.
followUp.why: It separates the immediate decision from information that can be read later.
followUp.delivery: Lead with the decision, use one short sentence, then pause for their answer.
